text.p: Guangshen Railway Co Ltd said on Tuesday that its chairman and chief accountant have been relieved of their duties after a Chinese government investigation into an allegedly improper investment.

Guangshen, a China-based company, said in a news release that Chairman Ge Wenan and Chief Accountant Zeng Xianshao were removed after the Securities Commission of the State Council of the People's Republic of China determined that they made an improper investment without the board of directors' approval.
The company said its foresees no difficulty in recovering the investment, which amounts to 300 million Chinese renminbi.
The investment was made with an independent financial institution, which the company did not name, in December 1996. It was made for a one-year period, and has been terminated, Guangshen said.

Guangshen said it had been notified by its controlling shareholder, Guangzhao Railway (Group) Co, that the parent company would propose to remove Ge Wenan and Zeng Zianzhao from the Guangshen board at the next shareholders meeting, on June 24.
A proposal will be made to replace them with Li Daihua and Yao Ziaocong, respectively. Yao Xiaocong already has been named the new chief accountant.
The company said it does not anticipate that its operations would be materially affected by the managment changes.

The company operates the railroad between Guangzhou and Shenzen in southern China. Its American Depositary Shares closed Friday at 23-7/8. Trading in these shares was suspended Monday pending the announcement about the investigation and the management changes.
